# `@warlock.js/ai-mistral`

Provider adapter for Mistral AI. Mistral exposes an **OpenAI-compatible** API, so `MistralSDK` is a **thin wrapper** over `@warlock.js/ai-openai` (the `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill) — it does not re-implement the wire protocol, streaming, tool calls, structured output, error wrapping, or token accounting. It builds one internal `OpenAISDK` pointed at Mistral's `baseURL` with `provider: "mistral"`, then layers on this provider's own capability inference + default pricing. Pair with `@warlock.js/ai` for the agent / tool / system-prompt surface.

## Construction

```ts
import { MistralSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-mistral";

const mistral = new MistralSDK({ apiKey: process.env.MISTRAL_API_KEY! });
```

`baseURL` defaults to `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` (the OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving `/chat/completions` and `/embeddings`). `provider` defaults to `"mistral"` and flows through to `ModelContract.provider`, `AgentReport.model.provider`, and logs. Override `baseURL` only to reach a Mistral-compatible gateway/proxy. Every other upstream OpenAI `ClientOptions` value (`timeout`, `maxRetries`, `defaultHeaders`, `fetch`, …) is forwarded verbatim.

## Producing a model

```ts
mistral.model({ name: "mistral-large-latest" }); // multimodal flagship
mistral.model({ name: "magistral-medium-latest" }); // reasoning
mistral.model({ name: "pixtral-large-latest" }); // vision
mistral.model({ name: "some-fine-tune", vision: true }); // explicit capability override
```

Returns a `ModelContract` you pass straight into `ai.agent({ model })`.

## Capabilities — what's auto-set

The wrapper injects **Mistral-aware** inference before delegating to the OpenAI adapter (the OpenAI prefix lists never match Mistral names):

| Flag               | Default                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vision`           | Inferred from the model name. `true` for the `pixtral` family and the recent multimodal generations (`mistral-large`, `mistral-medium`, `ministral-3`); `false` otherwise.    |
| `reasoning`        | Inferred from the model name. `true` for the `magistral` family and the hybrid `mistral-small` generation; `false` otherwise. Drives whether `reasoning_effort` is forwarded. |
| `structuredOutput` | `true`, unless `responseFormat` is forced to `"json_object"` / `"text"` (loose modes).                                                                                        |
| `promptCaching`    | `true` (inherited from the OpenAI adapter — read-side `cachedTokens` accounting).                                                                                             |
| `pdf` / `audio`    | `false` by default (opt-in `.model({ pdf: true })` / `{ audio: true }`).                                                                                                      |

**Override any flag explicitly** via `.model({ name, vision?, reasoning?, structuredOutput?, responseFormat?, pdf?, audio? })` — an explicit value always wins over inference. The known-family fragments live in `known-models.ts` (`inferVisionCapability`, `inferReasoningCapability`).

The headline `-latest` aliases are exported as `MISTRAL_MODELS` ({ chat, vision, reasoning, embedding }) for convenience — `mistral.model()` also accepts any version-pinned id (`mistral-large-2512`, `magistral-medium-2509`).

## Uses the OpenAI-compatible endpoint

Because Mistral speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions + Embeddings protocol, everything the OpenAI adapter does applies unchanged: streaming deltas + consolidated tool calls, `response_format: json_schema` structured output (override per model with `responseFormat`), `reasoning_effort` for reasoning models, multipart image input, and the neutral `Usage` breakdown (`input` / `output` / `cachedTokens` / `reasoningTokens`). See `@warlock.js/ai-openai` (the `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill) for the wire-level detail — it is identical here.

**No image generation.** Mistral has no OpenAI-compatible image endpoint, so `MistralSDK` intentionally does **not** expose `image()` — the structural absence is the capability guard (`ai.mistral.image(...)` is a compile-time error).

## Embeddings

```ts
const embedder = mistral.embedder({ name: "mistral-embed" });

const { vector, dimensions, usage } = await embedder.embed("Hello world");
const { vectors } = await embedder.embedMany(["doc 1", "doc 2"]);
```

`mistral-embed` is reachable through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings`; the embedder delegates to the wrapped OpenAI embedder.

## Pricing — per-model registry

The adapter ships a default registry (`MISTRAL_DEFAULT_PRICING`, USD per 1,000,000 tokens, with the 10%-of-input cache rate as `cachedInput`) so cost truth works out of the box, on agent reports and on each `model.complete()` / streaming `done` usage. Pass your own `pricing` to win per model id:

```ts
import { totalCost } from "@warlock.js/ai";
import { MISTRAL_DEFAULT_PRICING, MistralSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-mistral";

const mistral = new MistralSDK({
  apiKey: process.env.MISTRAL_API_KEY ?? "",
  pricing: {
    // USD per 1M tokens — contract rates win over the defaults.
    "mistral-large-latest": { input: 0.45, output: 1.35, cachedInput: 0.045 },
  },
});

MISTRAL_DEFAULT_PRICING["mistral-small-latest"]; // { input: 0.15, output: 0.6, cachedInput: 0.015 }

const { usage } = await mistral
  .model({ name: "mistral-medium-latest" })
  .complete([{ role: "user", content: "hi" }]);
console.log(totalCost(usage.cost));
```

Resolution at `model()` time: per-model `pricing` (`mistral.model({ name, pricing })`) > SDK-level `pricing` > `MISTRAL_DEFAULT_PRICING` > `undefined`.

- **Source.** https://docs.mistral.ai/inference/pricing plus the model pages under https://docs.mistral.ai/models (API ids and aliases), fetched 2026-10-17. Covered: `mistral-large-latest` / `mistral-large-2512`, `mistral-medium-latest` / `mistral-medium-3-5`, `mistral-small-latest` / `mistral-small-2603`, `ministral-14b-latest` / `ministral-14b-2512`, `codestral-latest` / `codestral-2508`, `mistral-embed` / `mistral-embed-2312`.
- **Not included:** Mistral Large 4 (public preview at a temporary sale price) and the retired Pixtral / Magistral models (no longer on the price list) — pass `pricing` if you still call them.

## Prompt caching

Mistral's Chat Completions accepts `prompt_cache_key` (https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/conversations/advanced/prompt-caching). Set `promptCacheKey` on the model to route related requests to the same cache; it is sent while the SDK keeps its default `"mistral"` provider label. Cached tokens come back as `usage.cachedTokens` (inside `prompt_tokens`, so `inputIncludesCache: true`) and bill at `cachedInput`.

```ts
import { MistralSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-mistral";

const mistral = new MistralSDK({ apiKey: process.env.MISTRAL_API_KEY ?? "" });
const model = mistral.model({ name: "mistral-large-latest", promptCacheKey: "conversation:42" });
```

## Errors

Raw errors are wrapped into the typed `@warlock.js/ai` `AIError` hierarchy by the wrapped OpenAI adapter (dispatch keys on `APIError.status + code`) — see the `handle-ai-errors` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill. HTTP 503 (and OpenAI's `server_is_overloaded` code) maps to `ProviderOverloadedError` (`code: "PROVIDER_OVERLOADED"`, `retryable: true`); every wrapped error carries `status`, `retryable` and `billed` (`false` for 401 / 402 / 403, otherwise `"unknown"`).

## When NOT to use this skill

- Image generation — Mistral has no OpenAI-compatible image endpoint; `mistral.image()` does not exist.
- Other providers — OpenAI `@warlock.js/ai-openai`, Gemini `@warlock.js/ai-google`, Anthropic `@warlock.js/ai-anthropic`, Bedrock `@warlock.js/ai-bedrock`, Ollama `@warlock.js/ai-ollama`.
- Raw `@mistralai/mistralai` SDK or Vercel `@ai-sdk/mistral` without going through `@warlock.js/ai` agents.

## See also

- The `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill — the wrapped adapter; identical wire behavior.
- The `run-ai-agent` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — passing the model into `ai.agent({...})`.
- The `pick-ai-provider` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — adapter comparison.

## Provider body options and token estimates

This adapter delegates Chat Completions to the OpenAI adapter, so
`providerOptions.openai.body` adds native Chat request fields. Other provider
keys are ignored. Plain-object fields merge one level deep with neutral options;
caller-provided keys win, while arrays, scalars and `null` replace the field.
The OpenAI adapter's protected conversation, tool and transport fields remain
protected here too. Send only fields supported by this provider; do not reuse
OpenAI-only bodies across a mixed-provider fallback chain.

Models from this adapter have no native `countTokens` method. Check
`model.countTokens` before using an optional native counting capability;
`sdk.count(text)` is a separate offline estimate.
